about: The interior of the trachea: the larynx with its vocal folds and cricoid, the C-shaped rings, the trachealis, the air column, the carina and the two main bronchi. The cartilages are drawn as simple shapes, the larynx is drawn with its epiglottis, arytenoid, corniculate and cuneiform cartilages but without the hyoid bone, which belongs to the skull's own atlas and is drawn when the Bones layer is on, and nothing here models voice, and a cough is shown only as a display index of the engine's cough drive (no airway clearance is simulated); activity is a display index of the engine's breathing signals, of swallowing and of that cough drive.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

WEST10.label: West JB, Luks AM. West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 10th ed. Wolters Kluwer, 2016.

parts.label: Larynx (Thyroid Cartilage)
parts.summary: The cartilage shield that guards the top of the airway
parts.function: The thyroid cartilage forms the front and sides of the larynx, open behind. During a swallow the larynx is pulled upward and forward and the airway closes beneath the epiglottis, so food passes behind it into the oesophagus. It rises in this view while something is being swallowed.

drives.note: The larynx is drawn up and the airway closed during the pharyngeal phase of a swallow.

A cough begins with the glottis closed and the larynx braced, and the larynx is the first place the reflex is felt. The weight is a display choice, not a measured quantity; GH14 describes the cough reflex itself.

parts.label: Vocal Folds
parts.summary: Two folds inside the larynx that narrow the glottis
parts.function: The vocal folds lie across the larynx and can be brought together to close the glottis or drawn apart to open it for breathing. They close protectively in a swallow, and their vibration in the outgoing breath makes the voice. They are not driven by the engine and are shown for orientation; they draw together while the larynx rises in a swallow.

parts.label: Cricoid Cartilage
parts.summary: The signet-shaped ring at the top of the trachea
parts.function: The cricoid is the only complete ring of cartilage in the airway: narrow in front and tall behind. It joins the larynx to the first tracheal ring and gives the airway a rigid start.

parts.label: Tracheal Rings
parts.summary: C-shaped cartilages that keep the airway open
parts.function: Sixteen to twenty C-shaped rings of cartilage hold the trachea open against the pressure changes of breathing. Each is open at the back, where the trachealis muscle closes the gap. They are passive and are shown for orientation.

parts.label: Trachealis
parts.summary: The muscular back wall that closes each cartilage ring
parts.function: The trachealis is smooth muscle bridging the open back of the cartilage rings. Its tone narrows the airway a little, and in this simulator it brightens when the airways are narrowed, as in bronchospasm.

drives.note: Smooth muscle contraction narrows the airway, and the trachealis shares in it.

parts.label: Airway Lumen
parts.summary: The column of air running down the trachea
parts.function: The lumen is the air passage itself. Air runs down it on each inspiration and back up on each expiration, warmed and humidified on the way. The stream is drawn down while the lungs fill and up while they empty, and stops in apnoea.

drives.note: More air moves along the airway when minute ventilation rises.
A narrowed airway shows as a more active, constricted passage.

parts.label: Carina
parts.summary: The ridge where the trachea divides in two
parts.function: The carina is the keel-shaped ridge at the fork where the trachea divides into the right and left main bronchi. It is rich in nerve endings that provoke a cough.

parts.label: Right Main Bronchus
parts.summary: Wider, shorter and steeper than the left
parts.function: The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and runs more vertically than the left, so it takes the larger share of the air and is where inhaled objects most often lodge. It leads to the three lobar bronchi of the right lung.

drives.note: The airway carries more air when ventilation rises.
Bronchial smooth muscle narrows the airway.

parts.label: Left Main Bronchus
parts.summary: Narrower and longer, angled towards the left lung
parts.function: The left main bronchus is narrower and longer than the right and passes beneath the aortic arch on its way to the two lobar bronchi of the left lung.

drives.note: The airway carries more air when ventilation rises.
Bronchial smooth muscle narrows the airway.

parts.label: Epiglottis
parts.summary: Leaf-shaped cartilage above the larynx
parts.function: The epiglottis is a flexible leaf of elastic cartilage behind the tongue. During a swallow the larynx is drawn up and the epiglottis folds back over the entrance, helping to keep food out of the airway.

drives.note: The larynx rises and the epiglottis tilts over the airway during the pharyngeal phase of a swallow.

parts.label: Arytenoid Cartilages
parts.summary: Paired pyramid-shaped cartilages at the back of the larynx
parts.function: The vocal folds are attached to the arytenoid cartilages. These cartilages pivot and slide on the cricoid, which opens, closes and tenses the vocal folds.

parts.label: Corniculate Cartilages
parts.summary: Small nodules on top of the arytenoids
parts.function: Two small cartilage nodules sit on the tips of the arytenoid cartilages, in the back of the folds that run to the epiglottis.

parts.label: Cuneiform Cartilages
parts.summary: Small rod-shaped cartilages in the aryepiglottic folds
parts.function: These small cartilage rods lie in the folds of mucous membrane that run from the arytenoids to the epiglottis, and they stiffen the folds.

parts.label: Vestibular Folds (False Vocal Folds)
parts.summary: Paired folds above the vocal folds
parts.function: The vestibular folds lie above the true vocal folds and close the airway more gently. They do not make voice sounds in ordinary speech.

drives.note: The folds draw together to protect the airway during a swallow.

parts.label: Laryngeal Ventricle
parts.summary: Recess between the vestibular and vocal folds
parts.function: On each side a small pocket opens between the vestibular fold above and the vocal fold below. It lets the vocal fold move freely.

parts.label: Rima Glottidis
parts.summary: The gap between the vocal folds
parts.function: The rima glottidis is the narrowest part of the airway in the larynx. It opens wide for breathing and narrows when the vocal folds come together to make sound or to close the airway.

drives.note: The gap closes during a swallow.
The gap opens and air passes through it as breathing deepens.

parts.label: Cricothyroid Ligament
parts.summary: Ligament joining the cricoid and thyroid cartilages
parts.function: A sheet of elastic tissue joins the front of the cricoid cartilage to the lower edge of the thyroid cartilage. It is the part of the larynx that can be reached through the skin in the midline.

parts.label: Thyrohyoid Membrane
parts.summary: Membrane joining the larynx to the hyoid bone
parts.function: A broad sheet of fibrous tissue joins the upper edge of the thyroid cartilage to the hyoid bone, and so suspends the larynx from it.

parts.label: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerves
parts.summary: Branches of the vagus nerves that supply the larynx
parts.function: Each nerve climbs between the trachea and the oesophagus to reach the larynx and supplies most of its muscles. The left nerve loops under the aortic arch and the right under the right subclavian artery.

parts.label: Tracheal Mucosa
parts.summary: The lining of the airway
parts.function: The mucosa is the moist inner lining of the trachea. It warms and wets the air, and its mucus and cilia trap particles and sweep them up toward the throat.

drives.note: More air passes over the lining as ventilation rises.

The irritant receptors that provoke a cough lie in the airway lining, so the lining is shown engaged while the cough drive is raised. The weight is a display choice, not a measured quantity; GH14 describes the cough reflex itself.

parts.label: Tracheal Wall
parts.summary: The layered wall of the windpipe
parts.function: The wall has a lining of mucous membrane, glands in the layer beneath it, a framework of cartilage and an outer connective tissue coat. Together they keep the tube open and clear it of particles.

parts.label: Ciliated Pseudostratified Epithelium
parts.summary: Lining cells whose cilia sweep mucus upward
parts.function: Most lining cells carry cilia that beat together and move the mucus layer up toward the throat. This mucociliary escalator removes trapped particles whether or not the body is breathing hard.

parts.label: Goblet Cells
parts.summary: Lining cells that make mucus
parts.function: Goblet cells release mucus onto the surface of the lining. The mucus traps dust and microbes so the cilia can carry them away.

parts.label: Seromucous Glands
parts.summary: Glands in the layer beneath the lining
parts.function: These glands release a watery and mucous mixture onto the surface through small ducts. They keep the lining moist and add to the mucus layer.

parts.label: Hyaline Cartilage
parts.summary: C-shaped cartilage plates of the wall
parts.function: The C-shaped plates keep the tube open against the pressure changes of breathing. They are open at the back, where the trachealis muscle closes the gap.

parts.label: Adventitia
parts.summary: Outer connective tissue coat
parts.function: The adventitia is the loose outer coat of connective tissue. It holds the trachea in place among the neighbouring structures and carries its small vessels and nerves.

parts.label: Vocal Ligament
parts.summary: Elastic band at the free edge of the vocal fold
parts.function: The vocal ligament is an elastic band that runs along the edge of each vocal fold. It vibrates when air passes between the folds and so makes the voice.

parts.label: Vocalis Muscle
parts.summary: Muscle lying beside the vocal ligament
parts.function: The vocalis muscle lies alongside the vocal ligament inside the fold. It changes the tension and thickness of the fold, and so changes pitch.
